sections.h2: Which Roxboro office takes a Person County value question?
sections.html:
The Tax Office at 13 Abbitt Street in Roxboro handles it. Mail goes to the Tax Assessor, PO Box 1116, Roxboro, NC 27573, and the number on the county's appeals page is (336) 597-1721.

The county reappraisal page explains where the money goes. Commissioners pick a rate each year after deciding what yield the budget needs for services including law enforcement, solid waste, emergency services, elections, the library, health and social programs, recreation and agricultural extension. That happens when the budget is finalized in June.

  • Email for informal appeals: tax@personcountync.gov, which the county calls its preferred route.
  • Mail: Person County Tax Assessor, PO Box 1116.
  • In person: the Abbitt Street office.

If you plan to sell, the same office can tell you the value on the record and whether a relief program touches the parcel.

sections.h2: What does Census data say about Person County housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table lists 19,023 housing units across 392.34 square miles and 16,063 households. Owners lived in 77.3% of homes, and the typical owner-occupied house was worth $213,900.

  • Estimated residents in mid-2025: 40,636, up 4.0% from the 2020 base.
  • Residents aged 65 or older: 23.4%, a group that overlaps with the elderly exclusion described below.
  • Median household income: $63,300 in 2024 dollars.
  • Mean commute: 30.9 minutes.

Those figures are survey estimates and say nothing about any one parcel. Your own assessed value, shown on the county record, is what the tax bill uses.

sections.h2: When did Person County last reset its values?
sections.html:
The latest reappraisal used January 1, 2025 as its value date. Notices of value were mailed February 1, 2025, and owners who disagreed were asked to send the form back before March 1, 2025. Those dates are behind us.

What remains useful is how the county says it arrives at a number: comparable local sales, the cost to rebuild, potential income, location, property type, and the age, size, quality, condition and style of improvements. An owner who finds the number fair does not need to do anything.

The state requires a reappraisal at least once every eight years, and a county may choose a shorter cycle (G.S. 105-286). Person's 2025 schedule of values stays the reference until the next one, so ask the office for that date. The property record card shows how a given house was priced.

sections.h2: How does the informal review work?
sections.html:
An informal appeal goes to the Assessor's office on the form attached to your value notice. County appraisers review it, so no board hearing is needed, and the county says most owners start here.

Reviewers may recheck year built, square footage, bathrooms and other features. Include a daytime phone number and every document you want considered. The county will not open the file until the completed form arrives.

The Assessor then writes to report any change. Filing informally leaves your right to a formal appeal intact, and you can decide after reading the reply.

The formal path goes through the Board of Equalization and Review, which first meets between the first Monday of April and the first Monday of May and hears requests made before it adjourns (G.S. 105-322). A next-level appeal to the state commission is due 30 days after the board mails its decision (G.S. 105-290). Ask for this year's meeting dates.

sections.h2: What relief does Person County list for homeowners?
sections.html:
Person's relief page describes three state programs for a primary residence only, with a filing deadline of June 1 and 2026 income figures as printed here.

Person County homestead relief for 2026, as printed on the county relief page
ProgramMain terms
Elderly or disabled exclusionIncome $38,800 or below; 65 or totally and permanently disabled before January 1; reduction of $25,000 or 50% of value, whichever is greater, on the home and one acre
Veterans exclusionHonorably discharged and 100% disabled from a service injury; $45,000 off the value of the home and one acre
Circuit breaker65 or disabled; five years of ownership and occupancy; income up to $58,200; tax limited to 4% of income at $38,800 or less, 5% above that; annual application

The circuit breaker defers the excess tax as a lien. Death of the owner, transfer of the property or ceasing to use it as a permanent residence triggers rollback of the last three years of deferred tax plus interest. When several owners hold title, all must apply and qualify, though a married couple holding as tenants by the entirety does not count as multiple owners.

The county also has a land use and deferral page for farm and forest land, where deferred taxes become due for the current year plus three prior years if eligibility ends. Applications for the homestead programs are available from the Tax Office.

sections.h2: What are the payment dates and interest rules?
sections.html:
One statewide calendar applies. Tax is due September 1 and is payable at face value through January 5, then interest begins January 6 (G.S. 105-360). The first charge is 2%, and from February 1 it is three-quarters of 1% each month or fraction.

  • Personal property listing runs through January 31.
  • A good-cause extension for an individual cannot go past April 15.
  • A mailed payment counts on its postmark date.

Ask the Person County Tax Office for its bill mailing date, payment methods and any prepayment discount for the year you are selling.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill in a Person County sale?
sections.html:
The lien for each year attaches as of the listing date, and penalties, interest and costs join it (G.S. 105-355). A buyer inherits unpaid tax unless closing clears it.

The closing attorney therefore asks the office for a payoff. If the current year is not yet billed, the parties usually agree on a split. A tax that is left unpaid can lead to a foreclosure suit, a courthouse-door auction and a redemption right before confirmation (G.S. 105-374).

  • Request a balance for each parcel, farmland included.
  • Ask about deferrals tied to relief or use-value programs.
  • File the paid receipts with your closing papers.

sections.h2: Which questions should I put to the Roxboro tax office before listing?
sections.html:
A short call can prevent a delay at closing. Write down the answers and give them to your closing attorney.

  • What is the assessed value on the record, and does the record match the house as it stands today, including any addition or demolished outbuilding?
  • Is there any balance, interest or prior-year bill on the parcel?
  • Did an informal appeal remain open when the last notice was mailed?
  • Does the property carry an elderly, disabled, veteran or circuit breaker benefit, and will the sale end it?
  • Are deferred taxes recorded against the land?

Ask the office how a change of owner affects any benefit, and remember the June 1 filing date printed on the county relief page.

faqs.q: Where do I send a Person County informal appeal?
faqs.a: Email tax@personcountync.gov, mail it to PO Box 1116, Roxboro, NC 27573, or drop it at 13 Abbitt Street. Include your phone number and supporting records.

faqs.q: What value date did the latest reappraisal use?
faqs.a: January 1, 2025, with notices mailed February 1, 2025. Ask the office when the next one is scheduled.

faqs.q: What income ceiling applies to the elderly exclusion?
faqs.a: The county page prints $38,800 for 2026, and owners must be 65 or totally and permanently disabled before January 1. Filing closes June 1.

faqs.q: How large is the veterans exclusion?
faqs.a: It removes $45,000 from the value of the home and one acre for an honorably discharged veteran who is 100% disabled by a service injury.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the January 5 deadline?
faqs.a: Interest starts January 6 at 2%, then three-quarters of 1% monthly. Continued nonpayment lets the county enforce its lien through court, so call early.
